subtitle: How a Kingdom Wove Lakes, Lands and Temples into Power

panels.shot: wide aerial of Dorasamudra with a vast shimmering tank beside temple towers
panels.action: Hoysala Tank Builder stands on an embankment overlooking a colossal reservoir that hugs Dorasamudra’s temple-studded capital amid green fields and rocky hills.

dialogue.text: In Dorasamudra, capital of the Hoysalas, even the city’s name bowed to a lake — and its waters quietly bound kings, temples and villages into one power.

i18n.hi: होयसलों की राजधानी दोरासमुद्र में, शहर का नाम भी एक झील के आगे झुकता था — जिसकी चुपचाप बहती धार ने राजा, मंदिर और गाँवों को एक ताकत में बाँध दिया।

panels.shot: slow push-in from the lake surface to the city skyline beyond
panels.action: Morning mist rises off the broad tank as Hoysala Tank Builder watches temple spires and palace roofs of Dorasamudra reflecting in the still water.

dialogue.text: Dorasamudra, in today’s Halebidu, was not named for a king or a god, but for a great reservoir. Why did water, not war or bloodline, define this royal seat?

i18n.hi: आज के हलेबीडु में दोरासमुद्र किसी राजा या देवता पर नहीं, एक विशाल जलाशय पर नाचा गया था। पानी ने, न कि युद्ध या खून की रेखा ने, इस राजसी आसन को क्यों तय किया?

panels.shot: medium shot of Tank Builder kneeling with a copper plate, tank behind
panels.action: Hoysala Tank Builder kneels on stone steps of a kalyani, tracing old Kannada letters on a weathered copper-plate grant as villagers draw water nearby.

dialogue.text: Copper-plate grants and carved stones speak of tanks, kalyanis, boundaries and lands. They show a kingdom where every drop was measured, gifted and fought over.

i18n.hi: ताम्रपत्र और पत्थर की लिखाइयाँ टैंक, कल्याणी, सरहदें और जमीन की बात करती हैं। वे एक ऐसे राज्य को दिखाती हैं जहाँ हर बूंद नापी, बाँटी और छीनी जाती थी।

panels.shot: wide shot of countryside with scattered tanks, fields and shrines
panels.action: From a rocky outcrop, Hoysala Tank Builder surveys a patchwork of terraced fields fed by multiple tanks, each with a small shrine or temple on its bank.

dialogue.text: Across Hassan and Mysore, inscriptions tie water to worship: tanks beside shrines, fields feeding temples, gifts of land and wet soil carved into stone forever.

i18n.hi: हासन से मैसूर तक, शिलालेख पानी को पूजा से जोड़ते हैं: देवालयों के पास टैंक, खेतों से मंदिरों को अन्न, गीली जमीन और खेत पत्थर पर सदा के लिए दान में खुदे हुए।

panels.shot: close-up on copper plate engraved with terms devadana, brahmadaya, agrahara
panels.action: Hoysala Tank Builder holds a gleaming copper plate; etched words like devadana and brahmadaya glint as his fingers hover over engraved tank descriptions.

dialogue.text: Here we read of devadana for gods, brahmadaya for Brahmins, agrahara villages turned to learned estates. Always, the grant mentions water: tank, canal, or wet land.

i18n.hi: यहाँ देवताओं के लिए देवदाना, ब्राह्मणों के लिए ब्रह्मदाय, और अग्रहारा गाँव विद्वान जागीर बनते दिखते हैं। हर अनुदान में पानी दर्ज है: टैंक, नहर या सिंचित जमीन।

panels.shot: wide shot of a bustling village assembly under a large tree near a tank
panels.action: Beneath a banyan beside a small reservoir, Hoysala Tank Builder stands among village elders as they gesture toward the tank, fields and temple in heated discussion.

dialogue.text: In these lands, power did not flow only from the palace. Nagara in towns, sabha and ur in villages appear in records, debating rights over tanks, bunds and plots.

i18n.hi: इन इलाकों में ताकत सिर्फ महल से नहीं बहती थी। नगरों का नगर, गाँवों की सभा और ऊर अभिलेखों में दिखते हैं, टैंक, बाँध और खेतों पर हक को लेकर बहस करते हुए।

panels.shot: medium shot inside royal hall, Tank Builder before a Hoysala king (unfeatured figure)
panels.action: In a pillared audience hall, Hoysala Tank Builder presents plans on palm-leaf to a seated Hoysala king, with courtiers listening as a miniature tank is sketched.

dialogue.text: “Maharaja, a tank here will turn dry acres into your temple’s food and your subjects’ grain.”

i18n.hi: “महाराज, यहाँ एक टैंक बनेगा तो सूखी जमीन आपकी देवालय की रसोई और प्रजा का अनाज बन जाएगी।”

panels.shot: low-angle wide of a tank under construction, workers on embankment
panels.action: Hoysala Tank Builder directs labourers stacking stone and earth to raise a massive earthen bund, while artisans mark out future temple platforms on the shore.

dialogue.text: So tanks rose: earth piled high for bunds, sluices cut, channels lined. The king’s order met village labour and guild skill, each expecting a share in the new water.

i18n.hi: तो टैंक उठे: बाँधों के लिए मिट्टी के टीले, निकासी के रासे काटे गए, नाले सजाए गए। राजा का हुक्म गाँव की मेहनत और शिल्पियों की कला से मिला, सब नए पानी में अपना हिस्सा चाहते थे।

panels.shot: close-up of inscription being chiseled on tank stone
panels.action: Hoysala Tank Builder watches a stonecutter carve details of a tank grant into a slab: donor’s name, extent of land, and duty of the ur to maintain bund and sluice.

dialogue.text: In stone, obligations are fixed: who desilts the tank, who repairs breaches, who uses the water. The ur, the local body, is bound to the reservoir and its fields.

i18n.hi: पत्थर पर जिम्मेदारियाँ तय हो गईं: टैंक की गाद कौन निकाले, टूटे बाँध कौन जोड़े, पानी कौन बरते। ऊर, यानी स्थानीय जनसमूह, खुद जलाशय और उसके खेतों से बँध गया।

panels.shot: wide shot of Hulikere stepped tank with shrines, Tank Builder descending steps
panels.action: At Hulikere, Hoysala Tank Builder walks down steep, ornamented steps flanked by tiny shrines, the tank’s calm surface ringed by carved niches and green orchards.

dialogue.text: At Hulikere and other kalyanis, water lies at the heart of carved stone. The tank is both reservoir and sacred mirror, feeding gods’ offerings and villagers’ rice.

i18n.hi: हुलीकेरे और दूसरी कल्याणियों में पानी खुद तराशी हुई पत्थर-कला का दिल है। टैंक एक साथ जलाशय और पवित्र आईना है, देवों की नेवैद्यम और गाँव वालों के भात को खिलाता हुआ।

panels.shot: medium shot in village granary near temple, Tank Builder with elders
panels.action: Hoysala Tank Builder stands inside a temple granary, stacks of paddy around him, as elders count measures and one points toward fields glistening from tank irrigation.

dialogue.text: When tanks held, harvests swelled. Temple granaries filled, festivals grew generous, priests, artisans and peasants ate from the same stored grain of irrigated land.

i18n.hi: जब टैंक भरे रहे, फसलें उमड़ीं। मंदिरों की कोठारियाँ अनाज से भर गईं, त्योहार भरपूर हुए, पुरोहित, कारीगर और किसान एक ही सिंचित खेत के भंडार से पेट भरने लगे।

panels.shot: tight close-up on Tank Builder’s thoughtful face, shadows of gathering clouds
panels.action: Hoysala Tank Builder looks up at a darkening sky over the tank, his brows furrowed, as wind ripples the water and farmers watch anxiously from the bund.

dialogue.text: But inscriptions also whisper of danger: years of scant rain, breached bunds, disputes over shares. When water failed, all this delicate balance strained and cracked.

i18n.hi: पर शिलालेख खतरे की फुसफुसाहट भी करते हैं: कम बरसात के साल, फूटे बाँध, हिस्सों पर झगड़े। जब पानी चूका, तो ये नाजुक संतुलन खिंच गया, दरक गया।

panels.shot: medium shot of local assembly mediating by the tank, Tank Builder between factions
panels.action: On the tank steps, Hoysala Tank Builder stands between two groups of villagers as elders of the ur sit in council, hands raised to settle how to divide scarce water.

dialogue.text: “We must share by turns, or the bund we built together will become our boundary.”

i18n.hi: “हमें बारी-बारी से बाँटना होगा, नहीं तो जो बाँध हमने मिलकर बनाया, वही हमारी सरहद बन जाएगा।”

panels.shot: interior temple shot, Tank Builder viewing inscription naming nagara and sabha
panels.action: Inside a Belur temple mandapa, Hoysala Tank Builder studies a pillar inscription listing nagara and sabha among those granting land and rights connected to a tank.

dialogue.text: These records show negotiated power, not a neat planned system. Town nagara, temple sabha, village ur — each appears by name, each claiming a voice over water and land.

i18n.hi: ये लिखाइयाँ तयशुदा, साफ-सुथरे नक्शे की नहीं, सौदेबाज़ी वाली ताकत की कहानी कहती हैं। नगर का नगर, मंदिर की सभा, गाँव का ऊर — सब नाम से दिखते हैं, पानी और जमीन पर अपनी आवाज़ माँगते हुए।

panels.shot: wide shot of Dorasamudra’s main tank with temple complex, sunset light
panels.action: At sunset, Hoysala Tank Builder stands on the great Dorasamudra tank bund as orange light bathes temple towers and irrigated fields stretching into the hazy distance.

dialogue.text: The Hoysalas never mapped water like a later empire. Yet here, by this lake, we see their real craft: binding capital, villages and shrines through shared reservoirs and land.

i18n.hi: होयसलों ने पानी को किसी बाद के साम्राज्य की तरह नक्शों में नहीं बाँधा। पर यहीं, इस झील के किनारे, उनकी असली कारीगरी दिखती है: राजधानी, गाँव और देवालयों को साझा जलाशयों और जमीन से बाँधना।

panels.shot: close-up of a Hoysala gold coin in Tank Builder’s hand with tank reflection
panels.action: Hoysala Tank Builder holds a small gold coin over the tank; its surface catches the reflection of temple and water, hinting at wealth resting on stored rain.

dialogue.text: Every coin of Hoysala wealth, every sculpture and festival, stood on this quiet base: tanks that turned monsoon into memory, and memory into enduring power.

i18n.hi: होयसला दौलत का हर सिक्का, हर मूर्ति और उत्सव इसी शांत आधार पर खड़ा था: टैंक जो मानसून को याद में बदलते थे, और याद को स्थायी ताकत में।

panels.shot: final wide shot of modern Halebidu landscape with ancient tank, Tank Builder ghostlike
panels.action: A timeless vision shows Hoysala Tank Builder, half-faded, overlooking the old tank at Halebidu as present-day fields, houses and tourists spread around ancient bunds.

dialogue.text: Long after the Hoysalas fell, their lakes still hold water and memory, reminding us that a state truly lasts only when it learns to store and share the rains it receives.

i18n.hi: होयसलों के गिरने के बहुत बाद भी उनकी झीलें आज तक पानी और यादें संभाले हैं, हमें याद दिलाती हैं कि राज तभी टिकता है जब वह बरसात को सँजोना और बाँटना सीख ले।

title_i18n.hi: वो झील जिसने दोरासमुद्र को नाम दिया

subtitle_i18n.en: How a Kingdom Wove Lakes, Lands and Temples into Power
subtitle_i18n.hi: कैसे एक राज्य ने झीलों, जमीन और मंदिरों से ताकत बुनी
